The three counters above are integers and a boolean — the left-hand filter panel accepts neither. This field reduces them to a single ladder so they can be filtered, and takes the WORST rung when a report is missing several things at once.

Every morning the system pre-builds yesterday's sheet from the figures it\n already holds: weather, energy by stage, performance, availability,\n downtime hours. The duty operator edits the dozen or so fields only they know, then closes it.

Used for the "by period" source, and for the "metering stage" source when the CUMULATIVE figure to date is wanted rather than the day's own — the report prints both today's loss and the year-to-date loss, from the same field, differing only in the range summed.

Only used when the source is "a single meter". Declare the LOCATION CODE where the meter sits, not the meter code — a location carries only one meter of each kind, so the location is what operators name and what gets printed on the report.

Address tags by CODE, not by record: a configuration profile has to work for every plant of the same kind, and each plant has its own set of tags. End with "*" to match several — "T*_P" is the power of every turbine.

Required when the code matches more than one tag. Summing turbine power into plant power is right; summing temperature is meaningless — so the system does NOT guess, and a code that matches several tags without this declared is reported as a missing declaration.

More than fifteen fields for the operator to fill in. At this point the report turns back into copying by hand, and people fill it in to be done rather than to be right. Look again at which fields the system already has.

A wind sheet and a solar sheet differ in what each line says, not in how the work is done. So the lines on the sheet are data — adding a third plant type means adding a profile, not writing another report.

Only used when the source is "Computed from other lines". Write it with LINE CODES, for example "100 * e_td / e_inv". If an input line could not be measured, this line also reads NOT MEASURED together with the missing code — it is not replaced by 0, because a ratio computed over a fake zero still produces a plausible-looking number.

Visual observation (sky 06–09, 09–12…) is WEATHER DATA — its home is the observation log, not the report sheet. But making the operator open two screens every morning means one of them gets skipped. This flag puts the field right on the sheet, and the system writes it straight into the observation log — one home, one screen.

A solar plant's sheet is not a vertical list: three panels — energy / hours / weather — sit side by side, then the constants and the KPIs, then the hourly energy band. The operator reads by PLACE — where a field sits is part of reading it quickly, so changing the layout changes reading speed, not just appearance.

The TOTAL row sums numerators and denominators before dividing, rather than averaging percentages — except the vendor column: that figure comes from the vendor with no numerator or denominator to sum, so its TOTAL is an average of percentages and is NOT directly comparable with the two columns to its left.
Pre-built by the system from the day's work orders and outage log. Edit the wording here; to rebuild from scratch, clear it all and press the button at the top — the system does not overwrite edits.

Each line below is a line on the printed sheet. Where the system can fetch the figure, declare where from; where only the operator knows it, leave “The duty operator fills it in”. The system counts the fields the operator has to touch — that number is a promise to them.
